Publish a compiled reference, and read one back

Source: R/md-publish.R
md_publish.Rd

md_publish() compiles a spec and writes it as a bundle; md_reference() reads a published bundle into the form npmatch matches against. This is PLAN.md section 7b's first tier: most users download a compiled reference, not the database.

Usage

md_publish(spec, root = md_path("publish"), con = NULL, set_latest = TRUE)

md_publish_pointer(label, spec_hash, root = md_path("publish"))

md_reference(
  label,
  root = md_path("publish"),
  spec_hash = NULL,
  build_index = TRUE,
  fetch = FALSE
)

Arguments

spec

An md_spec() with a label.

root

The publish directory. Defaults to md_data_root()/publish.

con

A connection from md_db().

set_latest

Point latest.json at this bundle.

label

A published label, e.g. "active-observed".

spec_hash

The bundle to point the label at.

build_index

Also build npmatch's blocking index (npmatch::np_ref_index()), so the result can go straight to the cascade. Needs npmatch, which matchdb only suggests; without it the index is skipped with a message.

fetch

Download the bundle first with md_fetch_reference(): TRUE always (a bundle already here and intact is not downloaded again), "missing" only when the label is not published locally.

Value

The bundle directory, invisibly.

For md_reference(), a list: reference (an np_reference), name_freq, token_idf, addr_freq (an np_addr_freq, when published), places (a list of the place, place_layer and place_unit rows for the bundle's places, when published), clusters (when published), ref_index (when built) and stamp.

What a bundle is

<root>/<label>/<spec_hash>/ holds

reference.parquet

the frame md_compile() returns

name_freq.parquet, token_idf.parquet

npmatch's corpus statistics for exactly that frame

addr_freq.parquet

address sharing over exactly that frame (md_addr_freq()): records per address and suite, suite coverage, name concentration and npmatch's place class

place.parquet, place_layer.parquet, place_unit.parquet

when md_build_places() has run: the evidence and flags for the places the frame touches, counted over the whole database

report.json

the compile report: shape and absence

stamp.json

the spec, the spec hash, the database fingerprint, the normalizer signature, the npmatch and matchdb versions, and the md5 of every file above

and <root>/latest.json maps each label to the bundle currently published under it.

Why the stamp is checked, and rollback is a pointer

A bundle's derived columns and statistics are only right for the normalizer that made them (section 9). md_reference() refuses a bundle whose normalizer signature is not the installed one, and one whose files do not match their recorded md5. Rolling back is editing latest.json back to an earlier hash - md_publish_pointer() - since every bundle stays where it was written (section 7d).
